title: The North Pacific sigma0 26.5 winter outcrop shrank 35-40 yr ahead of the bias-corrected CMIP6 forced path as it freshened; outcrop-scaled renewal gives the western AOU gain but 35-50% off California
abstract: Question: does the shrinking late-winter outcrop of the sigma0 26.4-26.6 class explain the oxygen (O2) loss on sigma0 26.5 in the North Pacific (NP) and at BATS, is the outcrop loss the forced response that climate models simulate, and what does it imply for the future? Approach: WOA23 decadal temperature and salinity (1955-2022) gave the outcrop area, mixed-layer class volume and March surface change in the NP and North Atlantic (NATL). For 12 CMIP6 models (one member each) we added the model surface temperature and salinity changes to the observed 1965-1984 state (delta method), for 2005-2022 and for SSP2-4.5 to 2100 (SSP5-8.5: 3 models). A renewal box model, with a ventilation rate proportional to the outcrop area and an oxygen utilization rate from independent tracer estimates, was compared with published AOU changes in 7 NP regions and at BATS. Results: the NP class area fell to 0.47 of 1965-1984 (area >= 26.5: 0.14); the NATL class west of 40 W to 0.72. Through the same steps, 11 of 12 bias-corrected models gave a smaller NP loss (median ratio 0.84, observed 0.53); the model median reaches the observed state only in about 2049-2055. The NP outcrop-box surface density fell by 0.145 kg/m3, half from warming and half from freshening; the model mean fell by 0.072, with warming but no freshening (z = -2.4). The NATL change agrees with the models. In SSP2-4.5 the bias-corrected NP class outcrop falls to 0.38 by 2051-2070 and is gone in 5 of 11 models by 2081-2100. With no outcrop-independent renewal, the model gave AOU gains of 16-25 umol/kg where 10-27 were observed at 160 E-130 W, but only 35-50% of the observed gain in the transition zone and off California, and 65% at BATS at the wrong time. If this scaling held, the projected outcrop loss would add about 51-59 umol/kg of AOU by 2041-2060 (22-42 with alternative assumptions). Limitations: WOA23 decades are smoothed and sparse before 1985; single model members; outcrop area is a proxy for subduction; one-box renewal; the implied AOU is a conditional bound, not an O2 projection; the NP freshening may be internal variability.
